author: reek
body: `read` and `write` were menu items the console could not perform. Both set a status saying "enter address" and nothing consumed the next line: it fell through to the address evaluator, moved the cursor, and no read or write ever happened. So this test is about the WIRING, and it is driven entirely through `handle-console-input` for the same reason `debug-expr` is -- calling the helpers directly would pass against the old arms too.

author: reek
body: The discriminating readings are the ones AFTER a refusal. A status line can say anything, so each refusal is followed by a read that shows what the byte really is:

author: reek
body: - an out-of-range value must leave the byte UNCHANGED, not store its low

author: reek
body: - a bad expression while the write is armed must cancel it, and the NEXT
